title: Rap vocal, jersey club drums
hook: Turning a rap acapella into a jersey club moment.
voiceover: Turning a rap acapella into a jersey club moment. Jersey club lives at 130 to 140 BPM. A 90s rap record lives around 90. You can't beatmatch those. What I actually do. I bring up a club track with a long drum intro, that Think break kick pattern everybody in Newark grew up on, and I drop the rap vocal over it for 1 line only, as a shout. Not a blend, a tease. The room hears a line they know over drums they're already dancing to, they scream, and the vocal's gone. Then I play the actual jersey flip of that record, the one the Jersey producers already made. Tease, then payoff. What rap line gets the biggest scream in your room?
caption: Saturday craft. You can't beatmatch a 90 BPM rap record into jersey club at 135, so don't try. Drop one line of the vocal as a shout over the club drums, let the room scream, pull it, then play the jersey flip of that record the Newark producers already made. Tease, then payoff. DJs, what rap line gets the biggest scream in your room?
subject: DJ Sliink
